clue.text: The result if one's had changes made

indicators.note: changes made to a set of letters rearranges them into a new order

parts.note: one's supplies its letters with the s included

explanation.surface: Someone muses on what would follow had they changed things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' signals an anagram of IF ONE'S HAD, nine letters; 'The result' is a link and 'made' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fashioned has been shaped or produced, a synonym of made.

clue.text: "O, what a godly outside hath!" (Mer, of Venice)

definitions.text: "O, what a godly outside hath!" (Mer, of Venice)

parts.words: "O, what a godly outside hath!" (Mer, of Venice)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word is what Antonio says wears a fair outward show in The Merchant of Venice

explanation.walkthrough: The full line in The Merchant of Venice is 'O, what a goodly outside falsehood hath!', Antonio's remark on Shylock quoting scripture; the clue prints 'godly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation's gap is filled by the word for a lie, which in the line is said to look fair from outside.

clue.text: Get an impression of sound intelligence

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to come across as a person of good intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: To get an impression is to perceive or feel; sound intelligence is good judgment or wisdom.

clue.text: Adult converse

parts.note: read as 'the opposite of grown-up', not as grown-ups chatting

explanation.walkthrough: 'converse' looks like a verb, grown-ups talking, but it is the noun meaning opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of being fully grown is being childish or undeveloped.

clue.text: Point to any port in a storm, being unaligned

parts.note: N, north, is a compass point

indicators.note: letters tossed in a storm are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Advice to head for any harbour at all when the weather turns rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a storm' rearranges ANY PORT into ONPARTY, which follows N; 'to' and 'being' are links. The surface plays on the saying 'any port in a storm'.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician not attached to any political grouping is non-aligned, independent.

clue.text: Dormant fancies

parts.note: imaginings had while sleeping, dormant meaning asleep

explanation.definitionFit: Visions experienced in sleep are fancies of a sleeper.

clue.text: Drink in the garden?

explanation.surface: An invitation to have a drink outdoors among the flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: A shrub is an old drink of fruit juice, sugar and spirit or vinegar, as well as a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fruit cordial and a bush growing in a border.

clue.text: Boxes, note, are in short supply

parts.note: to box is to spar, so boxes gives spars
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A list of boxes and notes that are scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly spread, scanty.

clue.text: Memo about a surplus

indicators.note: the memo word goes about, around, the a

parts.note: a memo is a reminder note

explanation.surface: A note concerning an excess of something.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over is the excess or residue.

clue.text: An animal can get thus absorbed in a waste-receptacle

indicators.note: taken into the receptacle, so the word for thus sits within it

parts.note: a bin is a receptacle for rubbish
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: An animal might end up swallowed by a dustbin.
explanation.definitionFit: The buffalo of the American plains is a large wild bovine animal.

clue.text: Row with employee on the railway

definitions.text: Row with employee on the railway

parts.note: a line is a row
a man is a worker, an employee

explanation.surface: A dispute involving a railway worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a straight line; the whole clue also describes a worker who maintains the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A track worker who maintains railway lines is a railway employee.

clue.text: The scholar's mathematical problems are returned

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: returned means the words are sent back, read right to left

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems

explanation.surface: A scholar's maths homework comes back marked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SUMS ARE round to give ERASMUS, the Dutch Renaissance humanist scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch humanist of Rotterdam was a celebrated Renaissance scholar.

clue.text: Having no list to put up

explanation.surface: Someone with no list to put up on the noticeboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' is a lean, as of a ship, not a written list.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no lean stands upright; to put up a building is to construct it.

clue.text: A large number charge for making introduction

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
a mission is a charge, a task entrusted to someone

explanation.surface: A big fee demanded for making an introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is entry or introduction into a place or society.

clue.text: A redoubt, properly built, could be difficult to shift

indicators.note: the letters are built properly, assembled into their right order

explanation.surface: A soundly constructed fortification would be hard to dislodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'properly built' rearranges A REDOUBT; 'could be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubborn, unmoved by persuasion.

clue.text: Dunderhead joining a union and hanging around

parts.note: read as head of dunder, its first letter
an alliance is a union

explanation.surface: A fool joins a union and loafs about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dunderhead' looks like a fool, but it splits as the head, first letter, of 'dunder'; 'joining' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance is idling or trifling, time-wasting.

clue.text: A little publicity — it's not way out

parts.note: an ad, a small advertisement, is a little publicity
it, with the 's read as 'is' linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A small advert insists that it is not the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: An adit is a horizontal entrance into a mine, so a way in rather than out.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine's horizontal entry passage is a way in, the opposite of an exit.

clue.text: Flat slates set askew

indicators.note: letters set askew are knocked out of line, rearranged

explanation.surface: Flat roofing slates laid crookedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat food is bland, lacking flavour.

clue.text: Found press unyielding

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that a press will not give.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rigid and inflexible is as hard as the metal itself.

clue.text: Strike makes the boards go about work quietly

indicators.note: the stage goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: the boards is theatre slang for the stage
OP is short for opus, a work
P is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: Industrial action leads stagehands to work softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt to work, an industrial strike.

clue.text: Stop holding the novice to be a fool!

indicators.note: the stop word holds the novice letter inside it

parts.note: a dot is a full stop
L is a learner, a novice, from learner plates

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone to stop the beginner acting the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolt is a stupid person, a blockhead.

clue.text: Over the river start to sow grass

parts.note: past means over, finished
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

indicators.note: the start of the following word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Instructions to begin sowing grass across the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastures are grassland for grazing animals.

clue.text: Some will sign it eagerly, but make light of that

indicators.note: some of the following words means a run of letters taken from them

explanation.surface: Some people will sign a document eagerly yet treat it lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks IGNITE from sIGN IT Eagerly; 'make light of' looks like trivialise, but means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something burning is to kindle a flame.

clue.text: Protective equipment that may show one's arms

explanation.surface: Protective gear that might leave one's arms on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' are a coat of arms, heraldic devices, not limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrior's defensive plate guards the body, and an escutcheon displays heraldic arms.

clue.text: The missile-launcher for which support's enthusiastic

parts.note: a sling is a support for an injured arm, with the 's kept
hot means keen, enthusiastic

explanation.surface: Keen backing for a catapult.
explanation.definitionFit: A catapult that hurls stones is a device launching missiles.

clue.text: Containers for coal fires

explanation.surface: Bags of coal for the fires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fires' is the verb, dismisses from a job, not burning grates.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal is delivered in large bags; to fire an employee is to dismiss them.

clue.text: Material giving offence

explanation.surface: Some fabric that causes upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Piqué is a ribbed cotton fabric; pique is resentment at a slight.

clue.text: Left nothing behind? Capital!

indicators.note: the nothing letter goes behind, after, the word for left

parts.note: quit means left, departed
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone who left nothing behind is congratulated: splendid!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like an exclamation of approval, but it is a capital city: Quito is the capital of Ecuador.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador's seat of government is a capital city.

clue.text: Put in prison, though not in favour of punishment

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a fine is a monetary punishment

explanation.surface: Jailed, despite opposing punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine is to shut up or imprison.

clue.text: Convert the property into cash — understand?

explanation.surface: A question about selling an asset for money.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise assets is to sell them for money; to realise something is to grasp it.

clue.text: A display of emotion in some dramatic work

explanation.surface: An emotional outburst within a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a fuss is an emotional outburst; a part of a play's act is a division of it.

clue.text: One guards ruins which may be unsafe

indicators.note: ruins as a verb wrecks the words, scrambling their letters

explanation.surface: A sentry who wrecks things could be risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangerous means hazardous, risky.
